summary: Iteration 24 tested four features: sharing a resource with no expiry, event reminders, event photos and the .ics calendar file. Backend: 18 of 18 pytest cases pass. POST /api/resources/upload gives 400 'Choose where to share it' with no destination, 400 for a bad share_cpd, bad hours or a blank title. All 4 share types create a CPD resource with a file in the right section. cpd_hours creates a My CPD log whose category matches the share type; with hours only the category is 'Course'. No certificate is created. The reminder loop was run in-process with notify and send_email mocked, datetime patched to 10am Perth and sleep patched. notify was called once, for Going and Maybe only (not not_going), with the title, the time ('tomorrow at 5:30pm') and the location. Check-ins were skipped. reminded_for stops a second reminder. Before 9am nothing is sent, and no email goes to @example.com users. Photos: not RSVP'd or not_going gives 403; Maybe, the organiser and admins are allowed; a PDF gives 400. ?token= serves the image bytes (401 without a token, 404 for an unknown id). GET event and GET events leave out storage_path. Deleting another user's photo gives 404; the admin and the owner can delete. ICS: a 5:30pm Perth event gives DTSTART ...T093000Z and DTEND +2h, an event with no time gives VALUE=DATE, no auth gives 401, an unknown event gives 404. Frontend (390x844, employee): the Certificate and 'Resource to share (no expiry)' chips work. Resource mode hides the issue and expiry dates and changes the title to 'Share a resource', the labels to Title/Provider and the button to 'Share resource'. With no destination it shows 'Choose at least one place to add it.' Sharing as Webinar created a Webinars resource (no Drive write) and returned to Home. The Events chips Upcoming / 'Past events & photos' filter correctly, and a past card shows '📷 1 photo · tap to view'. The detail screen shows the Google Calendar and Apple / Outlook buttons. 'Add photos' appears only after RSVP Going. Uploading 2 photos from the picker worked, the viewer opens, and the owner's delete works; a non-owner sees no delete. One real bug: the Google Calendar link has a zero-length date range for Perth users. No deprecated Expo packages were detected.

minor.issue: The content-type check trusts the client (anything starting image/), so image/svg+xml is accepted. GET /photos/{pid} then serves it inline from the API origin, which risks stored XSS (and the ?token= is in the URL). Allow-list jpeg/png/heic/webp/gif, or serve with Content-Disposition: attachment + X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Reference: /app/backend/routes/events.py:193-195,227
Removing a photo or deleting an event doesn't remove the objects from storage, so the files are orphaned (minor storage leak).
reminded_for is claimed before notify/send_email. If they throw, the reminder is lost for good (no retry). Acceptable, but worth knowing. Reference: /app/backend/routes/events.py:152-162

ui_bugs.issue: The end date is computed with `new Date(`${ev.date}T00:00:00`)` (local) followed by `.toISOString()` (UTC). In UTC+ timezones (Perth) the end date equals the start, e.g. dates=20261107/20261107; this was reproduced in a browser with timezone Australia/Perth. Google gets a zero-length or invalid all-day range. Timed events (5:30pm) are also added as all-day, with the time only in the details. Fix: build the end date with string or UTC maths (new Date(ev.date + 'T00:00:00Z') + setUTCDate). When parse_time succeeds, send dates=YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS/...(+2h) with ctz=Australia/Perth, the same as the .ics. Reference: /app/frontend/src/components/event-extras.tsx:18-24

issues: At 390px the 'Google Calendar' and 'Apple / Outlook' button labels wrap onto 2 lines. Consider shorter labels ('Google' / 'Apple · Outlook') or stacking the buttons.
The add-to-calendar buttons still show on past events, where they're pointless.
The photo trash button deletes straight away with no confirmation.

The certificate wording remains: the CPD switch subtitle says 'with the certificate as evidence', the 'From photos' tile says 'Photo of certificate', and 'Take a photo' says 'We'll fill in the details for you' although AI autofill is certificate-only.

action_items: Fix the Google Calendar URL in event-extras.tsx: compute the end date timezone-safely, and use timed dates when the event has a parseable time.
Restrict event photo content types (no SVG) and/or add nosniff + Content-Disposition when serving.
Optional: delete storage objects when photos or events are deleted; shorten the calendar button labels; hide the calendar buttons on past events; update the certificate wording in resource mode.
critical_code_review_comments: upload_resource never calls copy_cert_to_drive. It only writes to Drive when drive_spaces is sent (which was not done).
The photo permission (going/maybe/organiser/admin) matches between the backend and the frontend canAdd.
A past event where the user never RSVP'd doesn't allow adding photos, even if they attended. That's intended by the spec, but staff may not RSVP in advance.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all requested flows work; Google Calendar date bug in Perth timezone)

seed_data_creation: None persisted. Test events (incl. directly inserted reminder/check-in events), CPD resources/logs, 'New event'/'New CPD resource' notifications were deleted. Event photo objects in storage remain (no delete API for storage).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest tests/test_iter24_resources_reminders_photos_ics.py -n 0. The reminder test runs event_reminder_loop in-process with datetime/notify/send_email/asyncio.sleep patched. It uses a date 300+ days ahead so the real server loop and real events aren't affected. For UI data use `python tests/iter24_ui_seed.py seed|clean`. For Perth-timezone checks, open a new browser context with timezone_id='Australia/Perth'. Server clock is ~2026-10-28.
